subject: The eleven named steps of the implemented Product Alpha 001 synthetic learning loop.
authority_note: This assessment asks whether each implemented step would be the minimum effective solution in a real district. It is planning analysis over an already-built synthetic proof. It changes no Product Alpha runtime behaviour, records no accessibility or educational result, and authorizes nothing.
method: Each step carries explicit answers to the TDP-001 questions. The option set shown for each step is computed by the same deterministic evaluator used everywhere else in this register, so Option 4 cannot be presumed and cannot be hand-written.

records.reason: A list of who is being supported, on its own, is a list. It earns no database of its own: it is worth building inside SSLS only because the records it lists already need to be there.
records.data_needs: Names and current goal state for a small caseload.
records.deterministic_boundary: Ordering and filtering are fixed rules over stored fields.
records.human_review: None. Reading a list decides nothing.
records.prohibited_interpretation: A queue position is not a priority ranking of children and must never be presented as one.

records.reason: The detail screen is a projection of records the loop already holds. It needs no storage of its own and would not justify an application by itself.
records.data_needs: The learner's goal, observations, supports, and reviews.
records.deterministic_boundary: Everything shown is either stored text or a fixed derivation of it.
records.human_review: None. The screen reports; it does not conclude.
records.prohibited_interpretation: Nothing on this screen is an evaluation, an eligibility statement, or a service determination.

records.reason: A goal is the record everything else is judged against. It must survive staff turnover, keep its history, and stay connected to the evidence cited against it — which a document cannot guarantee.
records.data_needs: Goal statement, criterion, start date, review history.
records.audit_needs: Who set the goal and when it changed.
records.deterministic_boundary: The one-active-goal rule is a stored constraint, not a judgement.
records.human_review: The educator who sets the goal owns it.
records.prohibited_interpretation: A goal is not an individualized education program obligation and does not stand in for one.

records.reason: Observations are the evidence every later claim rests on. They must be append-only, time-stamped, and attributable, which a spreadsheet cannot enforce.
records.data_needs: What was seen, when, by whom, against which goal.
records.audit_needs: Append-only history; corrections recorded as corrections.
records.deterministic_boundary: Storage and ordering only. No scoring, no inference.
records.human_review: The recording educator is accountable for the text.
records.prohibited_interpretation: An observation is not an evaluation, an eligibility finding, a diagnosis, a disability label, or a discipline record.

records.surface: Plan a support that cites observations
records.reason: The link between a planned support and the observations that justified it is the whole point. That link is relational data, and losing it turns a plan into an assertion.
records.data_needs: Planned support, cited observation identifiers, planned date, owner.
records.audit_needs: Which evidence was cited at planning time.
records.deterministic_boundary: Citation integrity is a stored constraint.
records.human_review: The planning educator approves the support.
records.prohibited_interpretation: A support action is not a service determination, a placement, or an entitlement.

records.surface: Close off a support with what happened
records.reason: Whether a support actually happened, and when, is the fact that makes later follow-up evidence meaningful. It must be a record, not a memory.
records.deterministic_boundary: The clock invariant is a rule, not an opinion.
records.prohibited_interpretation: Completing a support proves delivery of that support only. It proves no benefit to the learner.

records.surface: Record what the follow-up evidence showed
records.reason: A follow-up is only a follow-up if it is provably after a completed support for the same learner and goal. That ordering constraint is exactly what a structured record enforces and a document does not.
records.data_needs: Observation bound to a completed support action.
records.audit_needs: The binding and its ordering are both recorded.
records.deterministic_boundary: The binding rule is mechanical; the meaning of the evidence is the educator's.
records.prohibited_interpretation: Follow-up evidence is not proof of causation and not a response-to-intervention determination.

records.surface: Review the goal against the evidence
records.reason: A review is a dated human judgement that later readers will rely on. It needs an author, an instant, and a correction path that supersedes rather than erases.
records.data_needs: Reviewer judgement, instant, reviewed goal and support.
records.deterministic_boundary: Supersession scope is enforced; the judgement itself is human.
records.human_review: The review is the human review.
records.prohibited_interpretation: A goal review is not an eligibility decision, a placement decision, or a legal record.

records.reason: The timeline stores nothing. It is an ordering of records that already exist and would never justify technology on its own.
records.prohibited_interpretation: Adjacency in a timeline is not causation.

records.reason: Once records are authoritative, keeping them intact under concurrent edits, corruption, and restore is not optional. The current browser-local implementation is a proof of the mechanics, not a district-grade answer.
records.data_needs: The whole document, plus a backup copy and a revision.
records.audit_needs: Conflicts refused rather than silently overwritten.
records.deterministic_boundary: Revision and digest comparison are mechanical.
records.human_review: A destructive restore is confirmed by a human against exactly what is on screen.
records.prohibited_interpretation: Browser-local storage is not backup, not durability, and not a district record-retention answer.

records.reason: The next step is fully determined by records that already exist, so it must be a fixed rule. This is the clearest case in the whole loop for deterministic logic and against a model.
records.data_needs: The learner's goal, observations, supports, and reviews.
records.audit_needs: Every projection names the records it was computed from.
records.deterministic_boundary: Total and explainable. Same records in, same step out, always.
records.human_review: The educator decides whether to act; the rule only proposes.
records.prohibited_interpretation: LLR-001 is not artificial intelligence, not a recommendation engine, not a risk score, and not a determination about a child.
